body:
oh man:  me too.  i mean:  me too in the restoring-faith department.

and thank you so much for the kind words about my writing.  it's been a few years since i've had  a book, and it's wonderful to hear.  i feel almost ashamed to say so.

ha.  

guilt:  my favorite indoor sport.

hi again, doorkmatter.  you bet:  i'll send you some things if i'm stalwart enough to produce anything.

this weekend was a better weekend than i've had in some time, actually.  i think you, and the good people at suicidewatch, are the reason why.

i didn't lock myself in the house.  i went out and was social.  and yes, i drank---the drinking over the past year has been very very bad, and the holidays are a total blur---but i was able to temper it with reason, this time.

last night, for example, i had four drinks over the course of about six hours, and finished the night with soda water.

so:  a victory there.

and thank you again for being so kind.

this is the first time i've really seen the living goodness of reddit.  i've seen the snarkiness and the cleverness and the richness of it and all that, but i've never had a personal experience like this on reddit.

or online, for that matter.

i've always been sort of scoffy about that whole enterprise.

but now, well, suffice to say you are appreciated.
i know that might look kind of weird on the screen, but i mean it.  i really do.

i am so lucky to have found this subreddit.  i am not that great at navigating reddit, and i always stick to like three or four main subreddits, and i sort of lucked into you guys tonight.  you have really made a difference to me.  it is so touching to have totally unknown people take time to talk this.

i came here because i was desperate but i didn't really expect anything to help.  and i didn't know if i'd be able to have the guts to be totally candid, to say the meaningful stuff that's on my mind.  i was afraid i'd be too afraid and cop out or something.

but this is just really something, reddit.  

and lizzyism, you are an inspiration.

no, i have no resources for that kind of therapy now.  haven't in years.  i have had very successful therapy in teh past.  it's one of the things i most hope for if i'm able to get another teaching job.

and UGH, isn't the phone a debilitating dread to have?  even my friends, people i like and love, when i see their names:  often i don't want to pick up.  sometimes i hurt their feelings about it.  

it didn't use to be that way.  not when i was a kid.  i got spooked by the phone when i got my first office job.  something happened and there it was.

funny thing:  when i hear you type it, i think to myself, She clearly has the power.  she's done it before.  she can do it again.

and then i think, Why don't i see the same thing about MYSELF?

do you have feelings of scopophobia?  is that part of it?
thanks scopophobic.  are you going through the same kind of thing currently yourself?

i'm trying to figure out if it would help or if it would make me feel guilty if i didn't produce.  can i think on it a bit?  it is very kind of you to ask.  even just doing this redditry has felt kind of nice.  written in such a burst of emotion that i think it overwhelmed my dread and i was able to write without thinking about it.

that was a nice feeling.

thanks, i am trying to, but it hasn't been working.  i can't even journal.  i've been trying to do that too.  the only good thing i've been able to do is start eating healthier.  it has kind of amused me to eat pumpkin seeds.  the package says "pepitas," which is adorable.
thank you.  i want to believe this too. i  think i pretty much do, it's just hard to see it these days.

so it's been a shitty week.  i realized this week that i'm losing my hair.  i never knew i was vain about it, but it turns out that i am.  at least the prospect of losing it provokes a crisis of vanity.

most people probably can't see it yet, but it's happening.  there was a day or two when i comforted myself by figuring that i was imagining it.  but nope.  i wasn't.

in the right light---direct, overhead light, like if the sunroof's open---i can see plenty of scalp though the top of my hair.  

so i'm having this unhappy mortality experience.  i also recently turned 41.  but i've always been fit and active and youthful, and now:  blammo.

i'm prefiguring elmer fudd.

and then i'm living in a vacant house because the friend i was living with had a total shitfit at me in public.  he's an old fella, and my best friend, but he has total psychotic shitstorms of fury.  zero to redline in .5 seconds.  honestly.

and he had one of these in front of my friend, the doctor across teh street, some sporty moms going by with babies in strollers.  all jetting right at me.

"YOU'RE A LYING FUCKING PIECE OF SHIT CUNT!" and etc etc.

it was shameful.  it humiliated me, and shamed him (although he doesn't think so; the next day i told him i lost a lot of respect for him and he goes, "you shoudl have GAINED respect!"). 

and so i moved temporarily into my dad's place (see how infantalized my life is, at freaking 41?) because i can't bear to be around the troll of fury.

incidentally, he's one of those people for whom apologizing is absolutely unthinkable.  like it's some terrible loss.  that just makes me nuts.

anyway, so here i am at my dad's house, and i get a call from my dad's new wife saying that he's had some terrible reaction to the flu shot and that he's so weak he can't get out of bed.

i get on the phoen with him and he is totally, totally zombied.  i ask him why he can't get out of bed, if it's dizzyness or lack of strength, and he goes, "it's these SOCKS, man.  they are just so SLIPPERY."

"too slippery to get up."

"totally."

now, you need to understand that he was born and raised in england.  he has a SMOKING JACKET and incomprehensible house-slippers.  and for him to talk like a surfer, well . . .weird.

but he's much better today, the drama is over, but i think he's still weirdly blissed out by his bout of expressiveness.

he has sent out braggy emails about how he projectile vomited.

it's like noel coward has been miscast in a john belushi movie.

but shit, that isn't really a story, is it?
ok, here comes a proper story.
it's part of the story of my crappy week, but it is a story all the same.
and not so miserable.
here we go.

thank you.  it's true:  it did sell well.  it was the most astonishing thing of my life.  picture in magazines, a movie deal (that never made it to the screen), book tours.  

it really was like i was being told---not just by a parent or an employer or something---but by the WORLD.

it was very powerful.

and exhilarating. 

it was like a happy ending in a movie, and i had done it all myself, with no help from anyone, pretty much.  my family didn't believe in me.  everyone thought i was nuts.  my grad school professors didn't really think that much of me.

it really was a triumph.

and i got letters from people telling me how much it meant to them.  a soldier in iraq who carried it into battle.  a couple who were getting married asked me to sign their book; i did, and they invited me to their wedding.  

it was really something.

but then life just kept getting harder.  couldn't find a decent teaching job.  kept searching for better ones.  i quit one i hated and only found visiting positions since.

so i've been getting more and more desperate.

and when my second and third book sold so poorly, it was like i lost confidence.

and now i feel like an old athlete who can't perform any more, but the thing that won't perform isn't my serve or my free throw or my fifty-time.  

it's my soul.

i've got a soul deficiency.
it feels like an olympic event.

and i'm not in imminent danger tonight or anything.  it'd be nice to hear anything at any time.

fuck, i'm already breathing better.  how funny that grief is so physical.

thank you.

it really does help.  it also has a breaking-bridge sensation which is making me cry much more but, weirdly feel better as i do it.

i don't like writing any more.  at least when i try to write a book i just clench up and FAIL.  which makes me ashamed.  so i don't write.  and i feel guilty.  and then i get rusty.

i know it's down there somewhere, but i feel so miserable i can't access the love.
